title: Finite residue extensions split into purely inseparable fibre-product points
statement: Let f:X→S be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], s∈S, n≥0 and points x:Fin n→X with f(x_i)=s. Assume that for every i the induced extension κ(f(x_i))→κ(x_i) [def-weil-residue-field] is finite. There exist a scheme U, an étale morphism φ:U→S [def-weil-etale-morphism], u∈U with φ(u)=s, integers m_i≥0 and points y_{i,j}∈X×_S U [def-pc-fibre-product], j∈Fin(m_i), such that each list j↦y_{i,j} is injective; p(y_{i,j})=x_i; q(y_{i,j})=u and the induced extension κ(u)→κ(y_{i,j}) is finite purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]; and for every point w of X×_S U with q(w)=u and p(w)=x_i there is j with w=y_{i,j}. No local-finite-type or isolatedness assumption is needed beyond the stated finiteness of the residue extensions; the input points need not be distinct.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 02LM, proof lines 12056--12089; the final verification uses Schemes, Lemma 01JT

proof.text: Identify κ(f(x_i)) with κ(s) using f(x_i)=s. Transport the finite extensions to κ(s), and apply the common separable splitting theorem to obtain a finite separable L/κ(s) such that every prime quotient of L⊗κ(x_i) is a finite purely inseparable field over L.
Realize L as κ(u) in an étale neighborhood φ:U→S, compatibly with the map from κ(s). Transport the tensor products, their spectra and the quotient extension properties across this field isomorphism.

The points over each pair (x_i,u) are in bijection with the primes of κ(x_i)⊗κ(u). Commute the tensor factors to compare with the tensors from the splitting theorem. The prime spectra are finite. Choose a bijection from Fin(m_i) for each i, giving y_{i,j}, injectivity of each list, the two projection identities and exhaustion.

The tensor prime quotient is already a field. Identify it with κ(y_{i,j}) compatibly with q by the fibre-product residue-field theorem. Transport finite-module generation and pure inseparability across that compatible field isomorphism.

theorem exists_etale_split_residue_points
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (s : S) (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → X)
    (hx : ∀ i, f (x i) = s)
    (hfinite : ∀ i, letI := (f.residueFieldMap (x i)).hom.toAlgebra
      Module.Finite (S.residueField (f (x i))) (X.residueField (x i))) :
    ∃ (U : Scheme.{u}) (φ : U ⟶ S) (u : U), Etale φ ∧ φ u = s ∧
      ∃ (m : Fin n → ℕ) (y : (i : Fin n) → Fin (m i) → ↥(pullback f φ)),
        (∀ i, Function.Injective (y i)) ∧
        (∀ i j, pullback.fst f φ (y i j) = x i) ∧
        (∀ i j, ∃ (hy : pullback.snd f φ (y i j) = u),
          letI := ((U.residueFieldCongr hy.symm).hom ≫
            (pullback.snd f φ).residueFieldMap (y i j)).hom.toAlgebra
          Module.Finite (U.residueField u) ((pullback f φ).residueField (y i j)) ∧
            IsPurelyInseparable (U.residueField u)
              ((pullback f φ).residueField (y i j))) ∧
        (∀ (i : Fin n) (w : ↥(pullback f φ)),
          pullback.snd f φ w = u → pullback.fst f φ w = x i →
            ∃ j : Fin (m i), w = y i j)
